survivors.claim: `--primary` values are matched against landed file paths byte-for-byte, with no normalization and no signal when a primary matches nothing. A primary written as `./spec/scripts/review-legs.js` (or as an absolute path) quietly falls back to the latest-review rule and attributes the row to a different spec. D1 says the value is a repo-relative path, so this is within contract, but `commit.md` has the session copy the path out of free prose (the /spec:fix statement or the commit body), where such spellings are likely.
survivors.impact: A slightly differently written file name in the fix description can still send the escape row to the wrong spec, which is the mis-attribution this spec exists to remove.
survivors.evidence: Executed: `node spec/scripts/commit-coverage.js --root . --commit 32b5af64 --primary ./spec/scripts/review-legs.js --json` returned pick {"file":"spec/scripts/init-gen.js","spec":"specs/20261029/08-the-policy-round-at-init.md",...,"reason":"latest-review"}. The same run with `--primary spec/scripts/review-legs.js` returned {"file":"spec/scripts/review-legs.js","spec":"specs/20261026/01-one-runner-for-host-commands.md","reviewRunId":"rv_50d84ff2d88f",...,"reason":"primary"}. Nothing on stderr warns about the unmatched primary.

survivors.claim: `--primary` followed by another flag takes that flag as its path. `--primary --json` exits 0, records the primary as `--json`, and prints the human render instead of JSON. D1's usage error only fires when `--primary` is the very last argument. `--commit` and `--root` already parse values the same way, so this follows the existing convention.
survivors.impact: A command with a missing path after --primary can quietly drop JSON output instead of failing with a usage message, and the commit step then skips the escape check.
survivors.evidence: Executed: `node spec/scripts/commit-coverage.js --root . --commit 32b5af64 --primary --json; echo exit=$?` printed the human render (`commit 32b5af640c43 — fix(spec)…`, `pick: spec/scripts/init-gen.js ← … (latest-review)`) and exited 0. Code: `} else if (a === '--primary') { if (i + 1 >= argv.length) die(...); primaries.push(argv[++i])`.

survivors.claim: No test exercises D1's several-primaries clause (latest review wins, tie goes to the lexically smaller spec path) or D2's tie-break. AC-1 passes one primary, and no fixture has two entries with equal review timestamps. I ran the multi-primary path by hand and it behaves as specified, so the gap is in test coverage, not in behavior.
survivors.impact: A later change could break how the pick chooses among several named files, or how it breaks ties, and no test would catch it.
survivors.evidence: D1 text: "with the latest `specs[0].reviewTs` when several primaries landed (tie: lexically smaller spec path)". AC-1's test uses `['--primary', 'src/x.js', '--json']` only. Executed: `--primary spec/scripts/review-legs.js --primary spec/scripts/init-gen.js` on 32b5af64 gave pick init-gen.js / specs/20261029/08 (reviewTs 2026-11-01T02:36:23.323Z, later than review-legs' 2026-10-26), reason primary, which is correct.

survivors.claim: Some asserts in the new tests use raw output (`r.stderr`) or a restated expectation as their message instead of a consequence-of-failure line. Examples: AC-3 and AC-8 `assert.strictEqual(r.status, 0, r.stderr)`, and AC-4 `'empty landed has nothing to exclude'`.
survivors.impact: When these tests fail, the message does not tell the reader what breaks, which the repo's test rules ask for.
survivors.evidence: Review Checks: "A new test whose asserts lack consequence-of-failure messages is soft". Lines added in the diff: `assert.strictEqual(r.status, 0, r.stderr)` (AC-3 and AC-8 tests), `assert.deepStrictEqual(none.ubiquitous, [], 'empty landed has nothing to exclude')` (AC-4 test).

survivors.claim: This review's patterns leg did not sweep any of the diff's code paths. `patterns.txt` shows `Scope: .claude specs/20261031`, but the range edits spec/scripts, git/commands, tests/commit-coverage and tests/commit. The `reconcile.json` the driver wrote has no `changed` key, so review-legs.js:429 got an empty changed set. The likely cause is that the driver ran an installed scope-reconcile.js older than the one that emits `changed` (7.293.0); I did not confirm this. review-legs.js predates the range, so this is not a defect of this spec. I swept the four directories by hand: no hit falls on a line the diff touches.
survivors.impact: The automatic pattern check reported clean without looking at the changed code, so its zero counts say nothing about this change.
survivors.evidence: legs-1/patterns.txt: `Scope: .claude specs/20261031`. legs-1/reconcile.json keys: outOfPlan, unrealized, excluded, renamed, atRisk (no `changed`). Executed: `DIFF_BASE=1814608a… bash scripts/spec-patterns.sh spec/scripts git/commands tests/commit-coverage tests/commit` gave hits only at smoke.sh:121, expire-tests.js:406, lib/scan-test-calls.js:23 and lib/app-port.js:26, none of them in the diff.
